mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated with FEDFUNDS declines, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals stronger demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the correlation is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises but S&P 500 returns are positive, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals stronger economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the correlation is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) show strength, it indicates a robust labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS are strong but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises but S&P 500 returns are positive, or the correlation is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and unemployment (UNRATE) is low, it may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the correlation is not significant.
